verses.greek: Ἢ ἀγνοεῖτε, ἀδελφοί, γινώσκουσιν γὰρ νόμον λαλῶ, ὅτι ὁ νόμος κυριεύει τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ἐφʼ ὅσον χρόνον ζῇ;
verses.literal: Or are you ignorant brothers — to those knowing for law I speak — that the law rules over the man for as long as the time he is alive?
verses.dgt: Or do you not know, brothers and sisters—for I speak to those who know law—that the law rules over a person for as long as that person lives?

verses.greek: ἡ γὰρ ὕπανδρος γυνὴ τῷ ζῶντι ἀνδρὶ δέδεται νόμῳ· ἐὰν δὲ ἀποθάνῃ ὁ ἀνήρ, κατήργηται ἀπὸ τοῦ νόμου τοῦ ἀνδρός.
verses.literal: The for married woman to the living husband has been bound by law if however shall die the husband she has been cleared from the law of the husband.
verses.dgt: For the married woman is bound by law to the living husband, but if the husband dies, she is released from the law concerning the husband.

verses.greek: ἄρα οὖν ζῶντος τοῦ ἀνδρὸς μοιχαλὶς χρηματίσει ἐὰν γένηται ἀνδρὶ ἑτέρῳ· ἐὰν δὲ ἀποθάνῃ ὁ ἀνήρ, ἐλευθέρα ἐστὶν ἀπὸ τοῦ νόμου, τοῦ μὴ εἶναι αὐτὴν μοιχαλίδα γενομένην ἀνδρὶ ἑτέρῳ.
verses.literal: Then therefore while is living the husband an adulteress she will be called if she shall become married to man another if however shall die the husband free she is from the law which not to be her an adulteress having become married to man another.
verses.dgt: So then, while the husband lives, she will be called an adulteress if she becomes another man’s; but if the husband dies, she is free from the law, so that she is not an adulteress if she becomes another man’s.

verses.greek: Ὥστε, ἀδελφοί μου, καὶ ὑμεῖς ἐθανατώθητε τῷ νόμῳ διὰ τοῦ σώματος τοῦ Χριστοῦ, εἰς τὸ γενέσθαι ὑμᾶς ἑτέρῳ, τῷ ἐκ νεκρῶν ἐγερθέντι ἵνα καρποφορήσωμεν τῷ θεῷ.
verses.literal: Likewise brothers of mine also you yourselves were put to death to the law through the body the of Christ for the to belong you to another to the One out from the dead having been raised so that we may bear fruit the to God.
verses.dgt: So then, my brothers and sisters, you also were put to death to the law through the body of Christ, so that you might belong to another, to the one raised from the dead, in order that we might bear fruit for God.

verses.greek: ὅτε γὰρ ἦμεν ἐν τῇ σαρκί, τὰ παθήματα τῶν ἁμαρτιῶν τὰ διὰ τοῦ νόμου ἐνηργεῖτο ἐν τοῖς μέλεσιν ἡμῶν εἰς τὸ καρποφορῆσαι τῷ θανάτῳ·
verses.literal: While for we were in the flesh the passions the of sins that were through the law were at work in the members of us to the bringing forth of fruit the to death
verses.dgt: For when we were in the flesh, the passions of sins that came through the law were working in our members to bear fruit for death.

verses.greek: νυνὶ δὲ κατηργήθημεν ἀπὸ τοῦ νόμου, ἀποθανόντες ἐν ᾧ κατειχόμεθα, ὥστε δουλεύειν ἡμᾶς ἐν καινότητι πνεύματος καὶ οὐ παλαιότητι γράμματος.
verses.literal: Now however we have been released from the law having died to that which we were bound in order for to serve us in newness of the Spirit and not in oldness of the letter.
verses.dgt: But now we have been released from the law, having died to that in which we were held, so that we serve in newness of Spirit and not in oldness of letter.

verses.greek: Τί οὖν ἐροῦμεν; ὁ νόμος ἁμαρτία; μὴ γένοιτο· ἀλλὰ τὴν ἁμαρτίαν οὐκ ἔγνων εἰ μὴ διὰ νόμου, τήν τε γὰρ ἐπιθυμίαν οὐκ ᾔδειν εἰ μὴ ὁ νόμος ἔλεγεν· Οὐκ ἐπιθυμήσεις·
verses.literal: What then will we say? Is the law sin? Never would it be! But the sin not I have known only except through law the then for covetousness not I had known only except the law was saying Not you will covet
verses.dgt: What then shall we say? Is the law sin? Certainly not! But I would not have known sin except through law. For I would not have known desire if the law had not said, “You shall not desire.”

verses.greek: ἀφορμὴν δὲ λαβοῦσα ἡ ἁμαρτία διὰ τῆς ἐντολῆς κατειργάσατο ἐν ἐμοὶ πᾶσαν ἐπιθυμίαν, χωρὶς γὰρ νόμου ἁμαρτία νεκρά.
verses.literal: An occasion however having taken the sin through the commandment it produced in me myself all covetousness apart from for the Law sin is dead
verses.dgt: But sin, taking an opportunity through the commandment, produced in me every desire, for apart from law sin is dead.

verses.greek: ἐγὼ δὲ ἔζων χωρὶς νόμου ποτέ· ἐλθούσης δὲ τῆς ἐντολῆς ἡ ἁμαρτία ἀνέζησεν,
verses.literal: I myself however was alive apart from law once when was coming however the commandment the sin revived
verses.dgt: And I once was alive apart from law, but when the commandment came, sin came to life,

verses.greek: ἐγὼ δὲ ἀπέθανον, καὶ εὑρέθη μοι ἡ ἐντολὴ ἡ εἰς ζωὴν αὕτη εἰς θάνατον·
verses.literal: I myself then died 10 And proved to be me the commandment that was to life this to death
verses.dgt: and I died, and the commandment that was for life was found to be for death to me.

verses.greek: ἡ γὰρ ἁμαρτία ἀφορμὴν λαβοῦσα διὰ τῆς ἐντολῆς ἐξηπάτησέν με καὶ διʼ αὐτῆς ἀπέκτεινεν.
verses.literal: The for sin an occasion having taken through the commandment deceived me and through it put me to death
verses.dgt: For sin, taking an opportunity through the commandment, deceived me and through it killed me.

verses.greek: ὥστε ὁ μὲν νόμος ἅγιος, καὶ ἡ ἐντολὴ ἁγία καὶ δικαία καὶ ἀγαθή.
verses.literal: So the indeed the law is holy and the commandment is holy and righteous and good.
verses.dgt: So then the law is holy, and the commandment is holy and righteous and good.

verses.greek: Τὸ οὖν ἀγαθὸν ἐμοὶ ἐγένετο θάνατος; μὴ γένοιτο· ἀλλὰ ἡ ἁμαρτία, ἵνα φανῇ ἁμαρτία διὰ τοῦ ἀγαθοῦ μοι κατεργαζομένη θάνατον· ἵνα γένηται καθʼ ὑπερβολὴν ἁμαρτωλὸς ἡ ἁμαρτία διὰ τῆς ἐντολῆς.
verses.literal: That which then is good to me myself became death? Never would it be! But the sin in order that it may be shown as sin through that which is good to me is working out death so that may become beyond excess sinful the sin through the commandment.
verses.dgt: Therefore, did the good become death to me? Certainly not! But sin, so that it might appear as sin, was producing death in me through the good, so that through the commandment sin might become sinful beyond measure.

verses.greek: Οἴδαμεν γὰρ ὅτι ὁ νόμος πνευματικός ἐστιν· ἐγὼ δὲ σάρκινός εἰμι, πεπραμένος ὑπὸ τὴν ἁμαρτίαν.
verses.literal: We know for that the Law spiritual is I myself however fleshly am sold under the sin.
verses.dgt: For we know that the law is spiritual, but I am fleshly, sold under sin.

verses.greek: ὃ γὰρ κατεργάζομαι οὐ γινώσκω· οὐ γὰρ ὃ θέλω τοῦτο πράσσω, ἀλλʼ ὃ μισῶ τοῦτο ποιῶ.
verses.literal: What for I do not I understand not for what I want this I do but what I hate this I do.
verses.dgt: For what I produce I do not understand. For I do not practice what I want, but I do what I hate.

verses.greek: εἰ δὲ ὃ οὐ θέλω τοῦτο ποιῶ, σύμφημι τῷ νόμῳ ὅτι καλός.
verses.literal: If now that which not I do want this I do I consent to the law that it is good
verses.dgt: But if I do what I do not want, I agree with the law that it is good.

verses.greek: νυνὶ δὲ οὐκέτι ἐγὼ κατεργάζομαι αὐτὸ ἀλλὰ ἡ οἰκοῦσα ἐν ἐμοὶ ἁμαρτία.
verses.literal: In that case now no longer I myself am doing it but that which is dwelling in me myself sin.
verses.dgt: But now it is no longer I who produce it, but sin dwelling in me.

verses.greek: οἶδα γὰρ ὅτι οὐκ οἰκεῖ ἐν ἐμοί, τοῦτʼ ἔστιν ἐν τῇ σαρκί μου, ἀγαθόν· τὸ γὰρ θέλειν παράκειταί μοι, τὸ δὲ κατεργάζεσθαι τὸ καλὸν οὔ·
verses.literal: I know for that nothing dwells in me myself That is in the flesh of mine good the for to wish to do is present with me the but to do the good not
verses.dgt: For I know that good does not dwell in me, that is, in my flesh. For the willing is present with me, but the producing of the good is not.

verses.greek: οὐ γὰρ ὃ θέλω ποιῶ ἀγαθόν, ἀλλὰ ὃ οὐ θέλω κακὸν τοῦτο πράσσω.
verses.literal: Not for that I desire I do good but that not I do want evil this I practice.
verses.dgt: For I do not do the good I want, but the evil I do not want—this I practice.

verses.greek: εἰ δὲ ὃ οὐ θέλω τοῦτο ποιῶ, οὐκέτι ἐγὼ κατεργάζομαι αὐτὸ ἀλλὰ ἡ οἰκοῦσα ἐν ἐμοὶ ἁμαρτία.
verses.literal: If now what not I do want this do no longer I myself who do it but that which is dwelling in me myself sin.
verses.dgt: But if I do what I do not want, it is no longer I who produce it, but sin dwelling in me.

verses.greek: Εὑρίσκω ἄρα τὸν νόμον τῷ θέλοντι ἐμοὶ ποιεῖν τὸ καλὸν ὅτι ἐμοὶ τὸ κακὸν παράκειται·
verses.literal: I find so the principle that which is desiring me myself to do the good that me myself the evil is present with.
verses.dgt: So I find the law, when I want to do the good, that evil is present with me.

verses.greek: συνήδομαι γὰρ τῷ νόμῳ τοῦ θεοῦ κατὰ τὸν ἔσω ἄνθρωπον,
verses.literal: I delight for in the law the of God according to the inward man
verses.dgt: For I delight in the law of God according to the inner person,

verses.greek: βλέπω δὲ ἕτερον νόμον ἐν τοῖς μέλεσίν μου ἀντιστρατευόμενον τῷ νόμῳ τοῦ νοός μου καὶ αἰχμαλωτίζοντά με ἐν τῷ νόμῳ τῆς ἁμαρτίας τῷ ὄντι ἐν τοῖς μέλεσίν μου.
verses.literal: I see however another law in the members of mine warring against the law of the mind of mine and making captive me to the law the of sin which is being in the members of mine.
verses.dgt: but I see another law in my members waging war against the law of my mind and taking me captive in the law of sin that is in my members.

verses.greek: ταλαίπωρος ἐγὼ ἄνθρωπος· τίς με ῥύσεται ἐκ τοῦ σώματος τοῦ θανάτου τούτου;
verses.literal: O wretched I myself am man! Who me will deliver out of the body the of death this?
verses.dgt: Wretched person that I am! Who will rescue me from this body of death?

verses.greek: χάρις τῷ θεῷ διὰ Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ τοῦ κυρίου ἡμῶν. Ἄρα οὖν αὐτὸς ἐγὼ τῷ μὲν νοῒ δουλεύω νόμῳ θεοῦ, τῇ δὲ σαρκὶ νόμῳ ἁμαρτίας.
verses.literal: Thanks be the to God through Jesus Christ the Lord of us! Then so myself I myself with the indeed mind serve law of God the but with the flesh the law of sin.
verses.dgt: Thanks be to God through Jesus Christ our Lord. So then I myself with the mind serve the law of God, but with the flesh the law of sin.
